context.full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
context.conclusion: V(K) is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W of V(K), if W is invariant under the induced operators x,y,h then W={0} or W=V(K). Equivalently V(K) is a nonzero irreducible L(K)-module.

record.definition: R=Z_(p)={a/b∈Q:a,b∈Z and p does not divide b}, with operations inherited from Q. A unit of R means an element having a multiplicative inverse in R.
M_R is the R-span of M in V, namely all finite sums of r_j m_j with r_j∈R and m_j∈M. The canonical map R⊗_Z M→M_R sends r⊗m to rm; its injectivity is to be proved, not assumed.
For i,j∈I, E_ij is the unique complex-linear map with E_ij(e_k)=δ_jk e_i for all k∈I, where δ_jk is 1 if j=k and 0 otherwise. This construction requires that e be a complex basis of V.

V(K)=M⊗_Z K. Here tensor products have their usual balanced-module meaning: they are generated by pure tensors subject to additivity in each argument and (am)⊗c=m⊗(ac) for the base scalar a∈Z, m∈M and c∈K. Induced lattice endomorphisms act on the M factor; the same symbols x,y,h denote these induced K-linear operators once preservation of M is established.

L(K) is the scalar extension to K of the free rank-three Chevalley Z-Lie algebra on formal basis ξ,η,ζ, with brackets [ζ,ξ]=2ξ, [ζ,η]=-2η, [ξ,η]=ζ, extended bilinearly and antisymmetrically with zero self-brackets. This is (Zx+Zy+Zh)⊗_Z K in the original notation, with ξ,η,ζ labeled there by x,y,h. These are abstract Chevalley generators, not their possibly nonfaithful operator images on V. The generators ξ⊗1,η⊗1,ζ⊗1 act on V(K) by the operators x,y,h induced from M. This is the Chevalley construction also in characteristic 2.

record.statement: Let A and B be commutative semirings, S a multiplicative submonoid of A, and B an A-algebra which is a localization of A at S. Let T be an additive commutative monoid and A-module. Then the A-linear map f:T→B⊗_A T, f(t)=1⊗t, is a localized-module map at S: (i) multiplication by each s∈S on B⊗_A T is a unit in its semiring of A-linear endomorphisms; (ii) for every z∈B⊗_A T there exist t∈T and s∈S with sz=f(t); (iii) f(t₁)=f(t₂) implies that st₁=st₂ for some s∈S. A localization B at S means the images of S are units, every element has a numerator in A and denominator in S, and equality of images of two elements of A is killed by some element of S.

record.statement: e=(e_i)_{i∈I} is a complex basis of V. For every integer t≥0, hy^t v=(λ-2t)y^t v; for t≥1, xy^t v=t(λ-t+1)y^{t-1}v. Also y^{λ+1}v=0 and all higher powers on v vanish. On the basis, xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ-i+1)e_{i-1} for i≥1, ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for i<λ, ye_λ=0, and he_i=(λ-2i)e_i. For all natural r and i∈I, X_r e_i=binom(λ-i+r,r)e_{i-r} if r≤i, and zero otherwise; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r} if i+r≤λ, and zero otherwise. All displayed divided-power coefficients are integers.

record.statement: The map R⊗_Z M→M_R, a_R⊗m↦a_R m, is an R-linear isomorphism, M_R has an R-basis indexed by I, and its complex span is V. Each X_r and Y_r for r≥0 preserves M_R. For all i,j∈I, binom(λ,j) is a unit in R, and E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1} X_{λ-i}(Y_λ X_λ)Y_{λ-j}. In particular every E_ij preserves M_R. More explicitly Y_λX_λ=E_{λλ}, X_{λ-i}E_{λλ}=E_{iλ}, and E_{λλ}Y_{λ-j}=binom(λ,j)E_{λj}.

For all i∈I, J_i=J; J is nonzero and finitely generated over R; M_R=⊕_{i∈I} J e_i inside V. The multiplication map Q⊗_R J→C, q⊗c↦qc, is injective and dim_Q(Q⊗_R J)=1. There exists b∈J with b≠0 and J=Rb, and for every such b, (b e_i)_{i∈I} is an R-basis of M_R.

The integer map Z→K extends to a ring map R→K by a/d↦(a in K)/(d in K). There are natural K-linear isomorphisms M⊗_Z K≃M_R⊗_R K≃(M_R/pM_R)⊗_{F_p}K, where F_p=Z/pZ and its map to K is induced by the integer map. There exists a K-basis β=(β_i)_{i∈I} of V(K), arising as the scalar extensions of b e_i for a nonzero b∈J with J=Rb, on which xβ_0=0, xβ_i=(λ-i+1)β_{i-1} for i≥1, yβ_i=(i+1)β_{i+1} for i<λ, yβ_λ=0, hβ_i=(λ-2i)β_i, with integer coefficients read in K. For every such basis define ε_ij by ε_ij β_k=δ_jk β_i. All binom(λ,j) and all r! for 0≤r≤λ are nonzero in K; induced divided powers satisfy X_r=(r!)^{-1}x^r and Y_r=(r!)^{-1}y^r in that range, and ε_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1} X_{λ-i}(Y_λX_λ)Y_{λ-j}. Thus every K-subspace invariant under x,y is invariant under every ε_ij.
